# C4 diagram syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-c4/grammar/c4.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

C4 syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `C4Context`, `C4Container`,
`C4Component`, `C4Dynamic` and `C4Deployment` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, apart from D452's changes, this file is fixed to match, and the parser
must match this file (DESIGN §4.4).

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text that no rule takes apart; and a line break appended. Keywords are case-sensitive.

Each statement goes on a line of its own, after the header line. A macro takes its arguments
in `( )`, right after its name: text, `"text"` (no escapes), `$name="value"` or an empty one;
commas only separate them. A boundary holds its statements between `{` and `}`, the first an
element, relation or style. As mermaid@12 lexed it, apart from D452: an unquoted argument stops
at `)` and at the line end, a `%%` comment keeps the line break after it, and a lone `title` is
a title with no text. A line holding `direction TB`, `BT`, `RL` or `LR` is one token that no
statement takes.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A C4 diagram is a header, a line break, then its statements: one or more, each on a line of
its own.

```ebnf
diagram = header nl statements EOF ;
```

`C4Context`, `C4Container`, `C4Component`, `C4Dynamic` or `C4Deployment`: the header, on the
first line. Every header takes every element.

```ebnf
header = C4_CONTEXT
       | C4_CONTAINER
       | C4_COMPONENT
       | C4_DYNAMIC
       | C4_DEPLOYMENT ;
```

Line breaks: a `%%` comment may come before each.

```ebnf
nl = [ COMMENT ] NEWLINE { COMMENT NEWLINE } ;
```

Statements, each after a line break; a title or accessibility line may be followed by an
element on the same line (`accDescr { … }` ends before the line does).

```ebnf
statements = otherStatement [ nl [ statements ] ]
           | otherStatement diagramStatements
           | diagramStatements ;
```

```ebnf
diagramStatements = diagramStatement [ nl [ statements ] ] ;
```

`title`, `accDescription`, `accTitle:`, `accDescr:` or `accDescr { … }`: the title and the
accessible title and description; the last of each wins.

```ebnf
otherStatement = title
               | accDescription
               | acc_title acc_title_value
               | acc_descr acc_descr_value
               | acc_descr_multiline_value ;
```

```ebnf
diagramStatement = Element
                 | Relation
                 | Style
                 | Boundary ;
```

`Person(alias, "Label", "Description")` and the other elements: `alias, label, descr?,
sprite?, tags?, link?`; containers and components take `techn?` after the label. A later
statement with the same alias merges into the first.

```ebnf
Element @Element = element arguments ;
```

```ebnf
element = PERSON_EXT
        | PERSON
        | SYSTEM_EXT_QUEUE
        | SYSTEM_EXT_DB
        | SYSTEM_EXT
        | SYSTEM_QUEUE
        | SYSTEM_DB
        | SYSTEM
        | CONTAINER_EXT_QUEUE
        | CONTAINER_EXT_DB
        | CONTAINER_EXT
        | CONTAINER_QUEUE
        | CONTAINER_DB
        | CONTAINER
        | COMPONENT_EXT_QUEUE
        | COMPONENT_EXT_DB
        | COMPONENT_EXT
        | COMPONENT_QUEUE
        | COMPONENT_DB
        | COMPONENT ;
```

`Rel(from, to, "Label")` and the other relations: `from, to, label, techn?, descr?,
sprite?, tags?, link?`; `RelIndex` takes an index first, which is not drawn.

```ebnf
Relation @Relation = relation arguments ;
```

```ebnf
relation = REL
         | BIREL
         | REL_U
         | REL_D
         | REL_L
         | REL_R
         | REL_B
         | REL_INDEX ;
```

`UpdateElementStyle(alias, …)`, `UpdateRelStyle(from, to, …)` and
`UpdateLayoutConfig(shapesInRow?, boundariesInRow?)`: style an element or relation already
written, or set how many shapes and boundaries go in a row.

```ebnf
Style @Style = style arguments ;
```

```ebnf
style = UPDATE_EL_STYLE
      | UPDATE_REL_STYLE
      | UPDATE_LAYOUT_CONFIG ;
```

`Boundary(alias, "Label") { … }` and the other boundaries and deployment nodes: their
statements go between `{` and `}`, the first an element, relation or style. The `{` ends the
macro's line or starts the next.

```ebnf
Boundary @Boundary = boundary arguments brace diagramStatements RBRACE ;
```

```ebnf
boundary = BOUNDARY
         | ENTERPRISE_BOUNDARY
         | SYSTEM_BOUNDARY
         | CONTAINER_BOUNDARY
         | NODE
         | NODE_L
         | NODE_R ;
```

```ebnf
brace = LBRACE nl
      | [ COMMENT ] NEWLINE LBRACE [ nl ] ;
```

The arguments, in `( )`: at least one.

```ebnf
arguments = argument { argument } ARGS_CLOSE ;
```

```ebnf
argument = STR
         | STR_KEY STR_VALUE
         | ATTRIBUTE_EMPTY ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`, `macro`, `attribute`, `string`, `string_kv`, `string_kv_key`, `string_kv_value`, `acc_title`, `acc_descr`, `acc_descr_multiline`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | direction_tb | `.*direction\s+TB[^\n]*` |  | `direction TB\|BT\|RL\|LR`: tried first, over the whole line from the token start (inside a label too). C4 has no `direction` statement: it is an error. |
| INITIAL | direction_bt | `.*direction\s+BT[^\n]*` |  | `direction BT`: an error, as `direction TB`. |
| INITIAL | direction_rl | `.*direction\s+RL[^\n]*` |  | `direction RL`: an error, as `direction TB`. |
| INITIAL | direction_lr | `.*direction\s+LR[^\n]*` |  | `direction LR`: an error, as `direction TB`. |
| INITIAL | title | `title(?=\n)` |  | `title <text>`: the diagram title, the rest of the line up to a `#` or `;`, trimmed. A lone `title` is a title with no text (D452). |
| INITIAL | title | `title\s[^#\n;]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | accDescription | `accDescription\s[^#\n;]+` |  | `accDescription <text>`: the accessible description, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | acc_title | `accTitle\s*:\s*` | push(acc_title) | `accTitle: …` and `accDescr: …` take the rest of the line; `accDescr { … }` runs to `}`. |
| acc_title | acc_title_value | `[^\n]*` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | acc_descr | `accDescr\s*:\s*` | push(acc_descr) |  |
| acc_descr | acc_descr_value | `[^\n]*` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | — | `accDescr\s*\{\s*` | push(acc_descr_multiline) |  |
| acc_descr_multiline | — | `\}` | pop |  |
| acc_descr_multiline | acc_descr_multiline_value | `[^\}]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `%%[^\n]*` |  | A `%%` comment after a statement, to the line end; the line break after it stays (D452). The parser keeps it as trivia; it is named here so the grammar can join the line breaks around a bare `%%` line. |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\s*(?:\n)+` |  | Line breaks, with the blanks before the last of them. |
| INITIAL | — | `\s+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | C4_CONTEXT | `C4Context\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | C4_CONTAINER | `C4Container\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | C4_COMPONENT | `C4Component\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | C4_DYNAMIC | `C4Dynamic\b` |  |  |
| INITIAL | C4_DEPLOYMENT | `C4Deployment\b` |  |  |

| INITIAL | PERSON | `Person\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | SYSTEM_EXT_QUEUE | `SystemQueue_Ext\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | SYSTEM_EXT_DB | `SystemDb_Ext\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | SYSTEM_EXT | `System_Ext\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | SYSTEM_QUEUE | `SystemQueue\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | SYSTEM_DB | `SystemDb\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | SYSTEM | `System\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | BOUNDARY | `Boundary\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | ENTERPRISE_BOUNDARY | `Enterprise_Boundary\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | SYSTEM_BOUNDARY | `System_Boundary\b` | push(macro) |  |

| INITIAL | COMPONENT | `Component\b` | push(macro) |  |

| INITIAL | REL_D | `Rel_D\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | REL_L | `Rel_Left\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | REL_L | `Rel_L\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | REL_R | `Rel_Right\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | REL_R | `Rel_R\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | REL_B | `Rel_Back\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | REL_INDEX | `RelIndex\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | UPDATE_EL_STYLE | `UpdateElementStyle\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | UPDATE_REL_STYLE | `UpdateRelStyle\b` | push(macro) |  |
| INITIAL | UPDATE_LAYOUT_CONFIG | `UpdateLayoutConfig\b` | push(macro) |  |
| macro | EOF_IN_STRUCT | `$` |  | The text ended right after a macro name. |
| macro | ATTRIBUTE_EMPTY | `\([ ]*,` | push(attribute) | `(` then blanks and `,`: the arguments, the first one empty. |
| macro | — | `\(` | push(attribute) |  |
| macro, attribute | ARGS_CLOSE | `\)` | pop pop | `)` closes the arguments (jison returned no token for it; D452 makes it the only way out of them but a line break). |
| attribute | ATTRIBUTE_EMPTY | `,,` |  | An empty argument: `,,` or `""`. |
| attribute | — | `,` |  |  |
| attribute | ATTRIBUTE_EMPTY | `[ ]*""` |  |  |
| attribute | — | `[ ]*"` | push(string) |  |
| string | — | `"` | pop |  |
| string | STR | `[^"]*` |  | An argument in quotes: no escapes, line breaks included. |
| attribute | — | `[ ]*\$` | push(string_kv) | `$name="value"`: a named argument. |
| string_kv | STR_KEY | `[^=]*` | push(string_kv_key) |  |
| string_kv_key | — | `=[ ]*"` | pop push(string_kv_value) |  |
| string_kv_value | STR_VALUE | `[^"]+` |  |  |
| string_kv_value | — | `"` | pop pop |  |
| attribute | — | `(?=\n)` | pop pop | A line break in the arguments leaves them, the macro open (D452). |
| attribute | STR | `[^,)\n]+` |  | An argument without quotes: to a `,`, a `)` or the line end, blanks included (D452). |
| INITIAL | LBRACE | `\{` |  | `{` and `}` around a boundary's statements. |
| INITIAL | RBRACE | `\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
